museum: Museu Nacional (Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro)
stated_count: at least 10 numbered specimens/boxes (Nº 234, 268-275, 277) described; no total stated
possible_additional_holdings: Childe's notebooks mention more wrapped examples originally (Santos & Locks 2005); Kitchen & Beltrão 1990 vol. 2 pp. 230-232 list crocodiles from the 1960 inventory (not seen). Official page mumias.html (search snippet only) says the museum kept a small collection of animal mummies incl. crocodile hatchlings.
scholarly_catalogue: Kitchen, K. A. & Beltrão, M. C. 1990. Catálogo da Coleção do Egito Antigo existente no Museu Nacional, Rio de Janeiro. Warminster: Aris & Phillips, 2 vols (vol. 2 pp. 211, 230-232 per Santos & Locks); Santos & Locks 2005
notes: Crocodile hatchling mummies (Fiengo collection, bought by D. Pedro I 1827) documented first-hand 1998-2005 by Santos & Locks (Locks = Setor de Arqueologia, Museu Nacional). Egyptian collection largely destroyed in fire of 2 Sept 2018 (c. 200 of >700 items rescued by 2019 per Agência Brasil search snippet); survival of the crocodile mummies not verified. Official site museunacional.ufrj.br/www.museunacional.ufrj.br unreachable in this session (curl TLS incomplete-chain error; WebFetch 503). Brancaglion Jr. et al. 2005 (J. Biol. Res. 80: 129ff) confirm 'human and animal mummies' generically. Status PROBABLE because of the 2018 loss; would be CONFIRMED as of 2005.

museum_original_name: Museo Provincial Emilio Bacardí Moreau (Museo Bacardí)
stated_count_source: González, Begerock, Leonard & Faltings 2020, Trabajos de Egiptología 11, p. 145: '...una momia humana (fig. 4) y algunas de animales (una cría de cocodrilo, un gato, un halcón y un ibis)'
possible_additional_holdings: News article (OnCubaNews 2024, candidate-only) lists 'un sapo, un gato, un ibis, un halcón y un cocodrilo' among mummified animals brought by Bacardí.
scholarly_catalogue: Lipińska, J. 1982. Monuments de l'Égypte ancienne au Palacio de Bellas Artes à La Havane et du Museo Bacardí à Santiago de Cuba (CAA). Mainz: Philipp von Zabern (not seen; classified part of Bacardí Egyptian material in 1970)
notes: Emilio Bacardí bought a human mummy and animal mummies in the Luxor market in 1912 (Begerock et al. 2021, Cuba Arqueológica 14(1): 33-46, p. 39). Begerock et al. 2021 (p. 41) state the Egyptian animal mummies are kept in the museum's deposits (not displayed) and that CT scanning is needed to determine their taxonomic identity. No inventory numbers or photo of the crocodile found. PROBABLE: species identification rests on the 1912 acquisition description; the Cuban Mummy Project (IECIM Madrid / Heidelberg HCCH) planned CT of the animal mummies.
